# Release v0.10.0

## Aprovação seletiva com espera obrigatória

Agentes podem autoaprovar manutenção compatível e conflitos de implementação com classificação de impacto, motivo, validação e registro de auditoria explícitos. Conflitos que afetam regras de processo ou resultados, conflitos incertos e desativações exigem revisão humana antes da implementação. Hooks nativos PreToolUse/Stop e a barreira do serviço mantêm o agente aguardando a decisão; silêncio ou tempo decorrido nunca concedem aprovação.

Definições preservam revisões antes/depois, hashes de fontes, autores, justificativas, decisões relacionadas, especificações e evidências de verificação. Use catálogo e histórico para investigar uma funcionalidade que parou de funcionar e relacionar uma regressão confirmada à mudança responsável. Observações geradas têm revisão opcional e não se tornam requisitos aprovados por uma pessoa.

## Seguir o idioma do VS Code

Controles e contribuições da extensão usam o idioma de exibição do VS Code: inglês ou português brasileiro, com fallback para inglês nos demais idiomas. O editor propaga uiLanguage e uma instrução de idioma para o contexto do projeto e hooks. Agentes devem escrever novas entradas da interface nesse idioma, preservando identificadores exatos, código e texto histórico. A documentação mantém os dois idiomas.

Gere com npm ci e npm run package:vsix. A saída é artifacts/contextory-workspace-0.10.0.vsix e seu .sha256 correspondente. Compare o checksum antes de instalar por Extensions > Install from VSIX e recarregue o editor/integrações nativas quando solicitado. Esta entrega gera o pacote local e envia commits de código; publicar assets de release no GitHub e instalar no editor ativo são ações separadas.

A validação cobre classificação e bloqueio de aprovações, histórico ligado às fontes, transporte do idioma, cobertura de traduções/substituições, interface inglês/português, consistência de skills e documentação bilíngue. # Release v0.9.0

## Revise conhecimento pendente em Approvals

Approvals é um destino principal ao lado de Work e Requests, com contador de pendências. Alertas e Review now abrem a fila diretamente. A consulta seleciona baselines observados e propostas pendentes antes da paginação; Knowledge continua um navegador independente para definições, histórico e cobertura.

Quando fontes mudarem, inspecione-as, informe um motivo e atualize o snapshot antes de aprovar a nova revisão. Atualizar mantém o item pendente. Erros locais explicam referências ausentes/conflitantes; motivos sobrevivem a navegação/falhas e envios duplicados são desabilitados. Isso não concede aprovação humana aos agentes.

## Explicações independentes e Carbon

Tools > Documentation busca explicações em inglês/português por assunto, caminho ou registro rastreado. Architecture oferece Explain this area; ações do pedido encontram documentação relacionada, incluindo vínculos nas specs descendentes. O contexto de origem recupera trechos relevantes mesmo antes de uma nova especificação ter associações explícitas.

A extensão/CLI inclui software-documentation 1.0.1, seus guias, o módulo Carbon 1.0.0 completo e fontes/tokens/modelos locais. Nenhum plugin separado é necessário. Três ferramentas Contextory fornecem leitura/guias/jobs, ações de geração/consumidor/Pages e associações observadas auditadas. Mudanças no texto, nas fontes e no conteúdo de registros marcam explicações vinculadas como desatualizadas.

A consulta funciona sem Python. A geração ocorre sob demanda com Python 3.11+ e lease atual para mutações; nunca bloqueia a inicialização do serviço. Corpora schema 1 podem ser consultados, e prévias/backups preservam conteúdo antes da geração Carbon schema 2. Publicar um projeto conectado continua uma ação explicitamente autorizada.

[Leia o fluxo de documentação](documentation.md)

## Instale e recarregue integrações

1. Baixe contextory-workspace-0.9.0.vsix e o arquivo .sha256; compare o SHA-256 antes de instalar.
2. Use Extensions > Install from VSIX e recarregue o VS Code ou IBM Bob. Reinicie integrações nativas quando solicitado para descobrir as ferramentas e skill atualizadas; a confiança permanece no cliente.
3. Abra Approvals para revisão humana pendente ou Tools > Documentation para consultar explicações. Python 3.11+ só é necessário ao executar operações de documentação.

[Baixar 0.9.0](https://github.com/igormicadei/Contextory/releases/tag/v0.9.0)

## Qualificação e escopo

As verificações cobrem a interface em barra lateral estreita e painel baixo, limites de revisão no backend, MCP/registro nativo, operações descartáveis e páginas Carbon offline nos dois idiomas em 1440/390/320 pixels. Recursos incluídos são verificados contra 469 hashes. A publicação compara VSIX/checksum baixados e o manifesto completo da documentação.

Node.js 24+ e workspaces locais confiáveis no Windows continuam o ambiente qualificado. Confiança de hooks, conversas autenticadas, outros sistemas e workspaces remotos preservam seus limites. Reutilizar metadados Contextory de projetos de referência permanece no backlog. Definições, releases e aprovações históricas são preservadas; explicações geradas não são requisitos aprovados.

# Release v0.8.0

## Console de trabalho e conexões confiáveis

Work e Requests concentram a interface na especificação atual e em um plano por vez. Tools abre a exploração do projeto sob demanda. A mesma view se adapta à barra lateral vertical e ao painel horizontal, preservando seleção, rascunhos e rolagem.

O progresso mostra evidências por critério, verificações em execução, bloqueios e trabalho recente em vez de estimar tempo. Alertas persistentes, badge e notificações deduplicadas destacam Knowledge aguardando revisão humana.

A recuperação detecta falhas de heartbeat e fluxos encerrados, reconecta com espera limitada e distingue limites de requisição. A inicialização independe de abrir a view. Até 256 receitas são aceitas; configurações inválidas preservam conexão e receitas válidas.

Reparos de hooks seguem a política de recarga configurada e a confiança permanece no cliente nativo. Snapshots processam arquivos completos em blocos de 1 MiB, inclusive acima de 20 MiB, e recusam mudanças durante a leitura.

[Instalar 0.8.0](install.md)

[Baixar VSIX e checksum](https://github.com/igormicadei/Contextory/releases/tag/v0.8.0)

## Qualificação e limites

A implementação passou em 115 testes de backend/core/integração/análise e 43 testes de navegador. Perfis isolados do VS Code 1.147.0 verificam ativação automática com Explorer visível, runtime reparado e inicialização pausada. O teste não chama extension.activate(). Um teste do pacote também verificou 33 receitas, preservação após configuração inválida e recuperação de serviço. Assets finais e Pages são conferidos separadamente na publicação.

Aprovação nativa de hooks e dispensa de notificações permanecem verificações humanas. Reuso de metadados de referências e documentação integrada permanecem no backlog; o estudo de viabilidade não implementa essas integrações.

# Skill de recuperação de código

## Skill de recuperação de código

Este é um recurso portátil de instruções distribuído sem alterações aos clientes suportados. O guia bilíngue vinculado explica sequência de tarefas, atualização das fontes, permissões e limites. Leia o SKILL.md instalado e suas referências ao aplicar a skill.

[Ler o guia bilíngue do fluxo](advanced.md)

Caminho do recurso canônico

```text
---
name: contextory-codebase
description: Understand a connected workspace, locate definitions and related code, assess source impact, and recover relevant project decisions through Contextory. Use for codebase questions and before changes spanning related components.
metadata:
  version: "9"
---

<!-- contextory-managed-codebase -->

Use the Contextory capabilities advertised by the current client. A connected MCP server or packaged CLI supplies shared retrieval; hooks and editor language services are optional. The same workflow applies in any agent.

When authoring UI-facing project records, read `uiLanguage` in `contextory_context_get` and use that VS Code language (`en`/`pt-BR`) for all new prose, even if chat uses another language. Preserve stored historical text, source identifiers and code; bilingual documentation keeps its paired locales.

In a multi-root editor workspace, first use `contextory_workspace_get`. Pass the intended `projectId` on every related retrieval and workflow call, with `workspaceId` when multiple editor contexts are attached. Omission/current stays on that server's project; changing the UI project does not change agent defaults. Keep project identity/root with records, artifact handles, graph snapshots and citations. Identical paths/symbols in different projects are distinct. Unknown or ambiguous scope fails instead of selecting another project. `codebaseId` still selects a read-only reference within the chosen project; references are not writable workspace members.

After resuming a chat, use its current advertised tools and a read-only probe before reporting Contextory disconnected; an earlier message or generated configuration does not establish current reachability. Report the concrete error or missing capability. In an editor, **Contextory: Check Native Connections** distinguishes current MCP/hook observations from history, and **Contextory: Restart Agent Extensions** reloads the Extension Host. Native project/hook trust remains with the client; reopening a session may still be required after tool changes.

For missing, stale or duplicate Contextory hooks, use advertised `contextory_hooks_rebuild` with the intended `projectId`, explicit native `provider` (`codex`, `claude`, `bob`) and a new `operationId`. It repairs managed hooks and the launcher without changing MCP configuration, other hooks or native trust. Inspect changed files and observations; an unchanged result is not proof of execution. Reuse the exact operation ID/input only to recover an interrupted call. If hooks remain unobserved after one repair, inspect native trust and service logs instead of repeatedly rebuilding. Codex approvals can differ for `C:` versus `c:`: review `/hooks` in the affected session using its actual workspace path. If MCP is unreachable, use **Contextory: Rebuild Agent Hooks** in the editor, then resolve any service startup error and reload the native session as needed. A rebuild cannot approve hooks or repair an unreachable service through MCP.

Start a code question or related edit with `contextory_code_context_get`: put the actual task in `query`, scope with known `paths` and optionally `specId`, and choose a bounded `budgetTokens`. Read the cited current files before deciding or editing. Read-only exploration does not require a tracked request.

Use `contextory_code_architecture_get` for orientation, `contextory_impact_get` for affected callers/dependencies/tests/records, `contextory_code_path_get` to explain a connection, and `contextory_flow_trace` for detailed branches/calls. Use `contextory_search` for earlier decisions, findings and changes, then inspect record state, revision and provenance. Resolve ambiguous symbols with `source:path#qualifiedName` where supported.

When something stopped working, recover its catalog contract and last known working source/check/version, then follow impact links, catalog before/after revisions (including agent auto-approvals), decisions and spec history. Search by feature and source path/symbol and page chronology. Treat these as candidate causes until reproduced; Git version membership and ledger recording intervals are different evidence. Link a confirmed regression/fix to the responsible change/spec/source and retain uncertainty otherwise. Compatible maintenance and implementation conflicts may be agent auto-approved; process/outcome conflicts require human review before implementation. Approval provenance never substitutes for executed checks.

Keep source citations, graph snapshot, coverage and truncation attached to conclusions. Narrow or page bounded results. Static calls, test references and inferred contracts are possible relationships, not proof of execution or test coverage. Generated facts do not become approved requirements.

Use advertised `contextory_catalog_get` alongside source retrieval to recover file responsibilities, rules/features, test links and UI layout/interaction contracts; inspect state, revision, pending changes and source freshness. Page `inventory:true` to identify files without descriptions. For documentation, `contextory_project_export` overview discovers all stored documentation datasets, with independent pagination for records, immutable revisions, history, relationships, source graph, checks/jobs, usage metadata and artifacts. Retain sequence/snapshot and provenance, and distinguish current approved behavior from observations and historical definitions. Read-only documentation needs no tracked request.

When advertised, `contextory_docs_get section=sections` retrieves authored project explanations by query, source path or local record ID, with stable page/section IDs, source freshness and observed associations. Follow `nextOffset` for coverage. Relevant explanations may accompany current-project code context; they remain separate from source facts and human-approved requirements. Use the `contextory-documentation` skill for authoring, migration, generation and maintenance with the bundled documentation/Carbon runtime. No separately installed plugin is required, and optional generation must not gate source retrieval or service startup.

For another local repository, use advertised `contextory_codebase_list` and `contextory_codebase_change` to register an authorized reference directory. Pass its `codebaseId` explicitly to source queries and flow expansion; omission/current always selects the active project. Reference graphs and project memory stay separate. Keep the returned codebase identity/root with relative citations. Analyzing a reference does not authorize applying its design, changing current requirements or editing either project. See the reference guide below for scope and freshness details.

Saved edits refresh the source graph automatically; re-query relevant context after saving changes. Task/impact/path queries also verify disk content. Use `contextory_code_index_refresh` to recover an empty/stale/failed index or import regenerated Graphify data; repeated refresh cannot resolve every dynamic/external gap. Unsaved editor flow overlays are separate from the saved-file graph. If a capability is missing, use the packaged CLI or native source tools and state the gap; do not invent tool calls. Preserve the user's scope and native permissions.

Read [retrieval and coverage](references/retrieval.md) for tool inputs, paging, freshness recovery and headless use.

For version-specific documentation, use advertised `contextory_version_get` and page each release's commits and semantic entries. Release entities and immutable revisions are also exported with project records. Git membership establishes which commits belong to a version; definitions/decisions associated by recording interval need that qualification. Local observed tags do not prove remote publication. This history is project-wide and needs no request/spec scope.

```

# Skill de migração de conhecimento

## Skill de migração de conhecimento

Este é um recurso portátil de instruções distribuído sem alterações aos clientes suportados. O guia bilíngue vinculado explica sequência de tarefas, atualização das fontes, permissões e limites. Leia o SKILL.md instalado e suas referências ao aplicar a skill.

Caminho do recurso canônico

```text
---
name: contextory-migrate
description: Build a source-backed Contextory knowledge baseline for an existing project, including file responsibilities, rules, features, tests and interface contracts. Use when bootstrapping or resuming a project knowledge migration; ordinary code lookups do not need migration.
metadata:
  version: "3"
---

<!-- contextory-managed-migrate -->

Act as the project's migration agent in the native client. Use the advertised Contextory MCP capabilities; never start a second model service or execute project modules to infer behavior. Migrating knowledge does not authorize changing application behavior. Preserve source, existing approved records, client configuration and historical decisions.

Use the project's `uiLanguage` from `contextory_context_get` for every new catalog title/description, finding, rationale, UI contract, review reason and report, even when chat uses another language. Preserve historical prose, exact identifiers, paths and code; reconstructed observations are not bulk translations of existing records.

Read `contextory_context_get`, recover the migration request/spec through search and inspect its current state. For authorized migration, create missing tracked work, attach this session and claim/renew the spec lease. If the tools are unavailable, report the missing capability and retain a source-cited draft; do not claim the ledger was populated.

Use `contextory_code_context_get` and inspect cited current source. Start `contextory_catalog_migrate` with `operationId`, `specId`, `leaseId` and a bounded `limit`. Resume with the returned `migration.id` in `migrationId` and a new operation ID, until `next` is null. After an interrupted call retry its exact operation ID/input, then inspect the run through `contextory_entity_get`. Its persisted manifest/cursor and skipped-file gaps are a file scan checkpoint, not semantic completion. Query `contextory_catalog_get` with `inventory:true` and page its independent record/proposal/inventory cursors to discover new or missing files after the scan. A later scan preserves existing descriptions.

Work through subsystems in bounded batches. Read file bodies, entry points, callers, docs, tests and earlier decisions. Replace generated symbol lists with concise explanations of actual file responsibility through `contextory_catalog_change` revision proposals. Record unknowns instead of inventing purpose. Register distinct rule and feature candidates with their source references and specific test file/symbol links, or `testGap` explaining missing validation. Reconcile contradictory implementation, documentation and tests as findings; describe observed implementation separately from intended behavior.

For every interface surface, inspect its layout and event/state handlers, and inspect the running UI when available and authorized. Add `category:"ui"` contracts with `ui.location`, `element`, `trigger`, `behavior` and `states`: placement/grouping, control/value, click/change/keyboard trigger, resulting action/state/persistence/navigation, and relevant initial/loading/empty/error/disabled states. Link behavioral tests or explicit gaps. Static extraction cannot prove pixel layout, dynamic dispatch or runtime effects; mark those limits with sources and follow-up findings. Projects without a UI should record why this category is inapplicable in the migration report.

Use leased `contextory_catalog_change` creates for new observations. Compatible corrections to file-purpose descriptions/source links can use `compatibility:preserved`, `impact:implementation`, `autoApprove:true`, the current revision and a source-backed reason; observations remain unapproved. Behavioral descriptions and UI contracts stay exact through auto-approval, even on observations. Implementation conflicts may auto-approve with a recorded rationale, but conflicts with process rules or results, changed behavior and retirements need a before/after human proposal before implementation. Link historical decisions/specs through `decisionIds` or `contextory_relationship_change`. Generated facts and legacy decisions never become retroactive human approval. Optional baseline review does not block migration. Wait on actual pending proposals; never borrow human credentials, infer approval from silence, or erase superseded/rejected history.

Before finalizing, reconcile the current inventory, stale/missing source fingerprints, duplicate descriptions, pending proposals, rule/feature-to-test gaps and interface interactions against the scope. Record a source-cited migration report explaining reviewed subsystems, omissions, conflicts, test gaps and categories not applicable. Keep resumable outstanding work when review is pending. Do not describe a completed file scan as a complete application specification. Run configured meaningful independent checks, map evidence to each criterion, include catalog IDs/explanation in the outcome, explicitly complete only verified specs and export the request report. No new application tests are needed merely to restate documentation.

For later documentation requests, use `contextory_project_export` overview and page the needed datasets (including immutable revisions, decisions, catalog entries/proposals, relationships, checks and artifacts). Use `contextory_catalog_get` for freshness and `contextory_entity_get` for exact revisions. Cite sequence/snapshot, approved versus observed state, evidence origin and coverage limits; omit superseded behavior from current instructions while retaining it in historical documentation.

```

```text
---
name: contextory-workflow
description: Track authorized software implementation in the connected Contextory companion. Use for requests, milestones, specs, issues, design decisions, evidence and continuing tracked work; ordinary questions need no new request.
metadata:
  version: "9"
---

<!-- contextory-managed-workflow -->

Requires the workflow tools advertised by a connected Contextory MCP server. Conversation, editing, model selection and permissions remain in the native client; the workflow is shared across agents. Ordinary questions need no new tracked work.

Read `uiLanguage` and `contentLanguageInstruction` from `contextory_context_get` before writing records. Write all new UI-facing prose in that VS Code language (`en` or `pt-BR`): titles, descriptions, criteria, findings/fixes, decisions/rationale, review reasons, catalog/UI contracts, outcomes and reports, even if this conversation uses another language. Preserve historical content and exact IDs, paths, symbols, code, commands and protocol keys. Keep documentation's required paired locales. Do not bulk-translate existing records; headless projects default to English unless an editor configured their language.

When managed hooks are missing, stale or duplicated, advertised `contextory_hooks_rebuild` repairs only the chosen project's native hooks and launcher. Pass explicit `projectId`, native `provider` and a new `operationId`; no spec lease is needed for this setup repair. Follow its trust/reload guidance and verify an observed hook event. Do not repeatedly rebuild an unchanged setup or edit global trust records. If MCP is unavailable, use the editor's **Contextory: Rebuild Agent Hooks** command and inspect service logs; native approval remains client-owned. See the codebase skill's recovery guidance for Codex workspace path casing.

For multiple workspace folders, read `contextory_workspace_get` and keep an explicit `projectId` on every related workflow/source call, adding `workspaceId` for ambiguous editor contexts. Each project owns its requests, records, sessions/leases, catalog, checks, evidence and releases. Never infer project identity from an ID, source path or the UI selector. For user-authorized work spanning projects, `contextory_workspace_request_create` creates linked local requests for explicit `projectIds` including this server's project. Implement each branch with its own milestones/specs, session, lease and evidence, then check the group with `contextory_workspace_get` and `groupId`. Partial/offline/missing branches remain incomplete. Retry partial creation only with the exact original operationId/input retained on the branch. Keep interface ordering explicit; there is no cross-project spec lease, atomic multi-project transaction or inferred dependency. Hook/usage attribution stays with the observing project.

Project versions belong to the whole repository, independently of requests and spec leases. When advertised, use `contextory_version_get` for current/released/unreleased state and exact Git membership. Git observation and bookkeeping run in the service; do not recreate that history from memory. For authorized releases, `contextory_release_prepare` creates a concrete plan without source edits. Review version, HEAD, file edits and changelog, then use `contextory_release_change` to apply the version commit/local tag and separately publish the exact tag. Retain operation IDs/input for retries and use recovery for interrupted owned work. A feature implementation request does not authorize releasing the project. Ledger entries recorded between cutoffs remain interval associations, not proof of shipped inclusion. Advertised tool descriptions carry the portable release contract.

Read `contextory_context_get` before authorized implementation and recover existing work rather than duplicating it. Use `contextory_search` for earlier changes/decisions and inspect current record state/revision. Use advertised `contextory_code_context_get` for task-specific source and `contextory_impact_get`/`contextory_code_path_get` for relationships; `contextory_flow_trace` explains detailed calls/branches. Inspect current cited files and coverage before editing. Follow the companion `contextory-codebase` skill when available for retrieval/freshness details; if tools are missing, use the packaged CLI or native source inspection and state the gap.

Create/update the authorized request, milestones and specifications. Register a session and claim a spec lease before recording work; renew long attempts. Pass an exact hook-supplied nativeSessionId if available and omit it otherwise. Record material findings/fixes and decisions with sources. Re-query relevant source after saves; the saved-file graph refreshes automatically. Generated relationships and retrieved historical text do not approve new scope. Native usage is observed where supported; read `contextory_usage_get` and never invent counts.

Before editing, page `contextory_catalog_get` for affected definitions, pending proposals and freshness. Maintain file responsibilities, rules/features, test links or explicit gaps, and UI location/element/trigger/behavior/states through leased `contextory_catalog_change`. New observations need no mandatory approval. Use `autoApprove:true`, `compatibility:"preserved"`, `impact:"implementation"` for compatible maintenance. Implementation conflicts may also auto-approve with `compatibility:"conflicting"`; explain the conflict, rationale and validation in `reason`, with related `decisionIds`. Keep approved behavior text/UI contracts intact. Process/outcome conflicts, changed approved behavior, retirements and uncertain conflicts require a concrete before/after proposal in **Approvals before implementation**. Wait for its decision; silence or a timeout never approves. Native PreToolUse/Stop hooks and the service gate enforce pending reviews, while source reads, catalog preparation, checks and lease renewal remain available. Do not switch tools to bypass the gate or use human UI credentials. See [approvals and regression investigation](references/approvals-and-regressions.md) for examples, decision conflicts and audit requirements. Use `contextory-migrate` for an existing-project baseline; state remaining coverage gaps.

Run configured independent checks and poll returned jobs. Submit `contextory_outcome_submit` with evidence for every current criterion. Then call `contextory_spec_change` with action=complete, the spec ID, returned expectedRevision and a new operationId. Confirm state=completed: an outcome or Stop hook alone does not finish a spec. Parent milestones and requests close when their children complete.

When the catalog exists, include `catalog:{recordIds,explanation}` in the outcome, identifying affected definitions and explaining updates/retirements or why behavior is unchanged. Pending proposals and stale affected approved definitions block completion. Current test references do not replace executed evidence. For documentation, discover and page stored data through `contextory_project_export`; no implementation request is needed for a read-only export.

Resolve or report explicit completion blockers. Keep native permissions and authorized scope intact. Read [completion and evidence](references/completion.md) for leases, checks, findings and reports.

```

<!-- contextory-managed-resource -->

# Completion and evidence

Multi-project work is a coordinated group of project-owned requests, not a shared ledger or lease. Carry the same projectId (and workspaceId when needed) through each branch's session, spec lease, findings, catalog, checks, evidence, outcome, completion and report export. Evidence and record IDs from another project cannot complete a branch. After every local request completes, query contextory_workspace_get with groupId; offline, detached or missing branches remain explicitly incomplete. Recover partial creation with its exact original operationId/input; each branch retains that input. Native hook/model/usage observations are not reassigned across projects by inference.

Recover earlier work with focused search and read its current request/spec state before creating records. Read cited historical revisions for rationale, then check whether later decisions supersede them. Keep observations, generated source relationships and approved criteria distinct. Hooks can restore reminders after compaction but do not carry the full current contract; reread `contextory_context_get` for it.

Attach a Contextory session with `contextory_session_attach`; never guess a native session ID. Claim/renew with `contextory_spec_lease`. Mutations require fresh revisions and unique operation IDs. Read the record after a conflict rather than replaying a changed mutation with an old idempotency key.

Record issues through `contextory_finding_record`, explaining impact, resolution and relevant sources. Blocking findings must be resolved before completion. Record concise choices and tradeoffs through `contextory_decision_record`. These explanations are project records, not chat transcripts.

Use `contextory_check_run` recipes and poll with `contextory_entity_get`. With no recipes, configure the project's existing meaningful check command in workspace `contextory.checks`, then reread context. If no meaningful check is available, report verification as pending. Agent-reported external results remain reported evidence and cannot substitute for an independent runner's passing result.

An outcome maps every acceptance criterion exactly once to current evidence. Finish source/configuration edits before final independent checks: evidence is bound to the source fingerprint, contract and attempt, so later changes may require new checks. A static test-reference edge is not test execution evidence. Explain changes, issues/fixes, decisions, validation and remaining limits, including when there were no findings or new decisions. Submit the outcome, explicitly complete the spec with the returned revision, and confirm its state. Export the full request using `contextory_report_export`.

Use only advertised workflow mutations. If a required workflow tool or connection is unavailable, preserve the work and explicitly report which tracking or verification step remains pending; native source inspection can continue within the authorized scope. Never pretend an unavailable call succeeded or that a hook completed a spec.

When a project catalog exists, include `catalog:{recordIds,explanation}` in the outcome. Explain additions, human-reviewed behavior changes, agent auto-approved maintenance/conflicts, retirements or why behavior is unchanged. Pending project proposals and stale affected approved source/test references block submission/completion. Refresh compatible source links through the leased auto-approval path, retaining the approved contract and original review; a changed hash alone is not a changed requirement. Observed baselines have optional review. A definition revision after submission invalidates its accounted outcome. Human review remains in Approvals for process/outcome conflicts and changed behavior; never borrow UI credentials. Page `contextory_project_export` for the complete stored base and immutable revisions. Follow [approvals and regression investigation](approvals-and-regressions.md) when classifying changes or tracing failures.

<!-- contextory-managed-resource -->

# Retrieval and coverage

## Hook recovery

Use `contextory_hooks_rebuild` only for an intended project's missing, stale or duplicate managed hooks: `{ "projectId": "<project>", "provider": "codex", "operationId": "<new unique ID>" }`. Supported providers are `codex`, `claude` and `bob`; Generic MCP has no hooks. The response separates changed hook files, launcher restoration and current-service MCP/hook observations. It never reads or writes native approval records, global hooks, MCP configuration or portable skills. Keep the exact operation ID/input for an interrupted retry; a later repair needs a new ID. Project/workspace scope is unchanged and reference codebases cannot be repaired through this tool.

If files are unchanged but hooks remain unobserved, review native trust and reload the affected session instead of issuing more rebuilds. The installed Codex client may distinguish `C:\\` and `c:\\` when looking up hook approval: use `/hooks` from the affected session's actual project path. When MCP is unavailable, the editor's **Contextory: Rebuild Agent Hooks** command or sidebar **Rebuild hooks** action can initiate recovery after the local service starts. Inspect service output if startup itself fails; rebuilding through MCP requires a reachable service.

## Choose the lookup

| Need                                                | Tool and useful inputs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Workspace contracts, active work, configured checks | `contextory_context_get`, optionally `specId`. This brief is cached orientation, not a fresh source investigation.                                                                                                                                                     |
| Locate code for a task                              | `contextory_code_context_get` with `query`, known `paths`, optional `specId` and `budgetTokens` (512–6000, default 3000). Exact definitions rank before mentions; neighborhoods and linked project records are bounded.                                                |
| Understand subsystems and entry points              | `contextory_code_architecture_get`. Default `refresh:true` verifies saved source; use `refresh:false` only when a cached overview is sufficient.                                                                                                                       |
| Find callers, dependencies, tests or linked work    | `contextory_impact_get` with `id`, `direction` (`reverse` for dependents, `forward` for dependencies, `both` for surrounding relationships), `depth` and `limit`.                                                                                                      |
| Explain how two things connect                      | `contextory_code_path_get` with `from`, `to`, optional `direction` (`forward` or `both`) and `maxDepth`. Returned edges retain their original direction.                                                                                                               |
| Inspect calls or branches                           | `contextory_flow_trace` with `root:{path,symbol}` or a zero-based position, `view: calls/flow`, `direction: outgoing/incoming`, and optional limits. Supported engines cover TS/JS and Python.                                                                         |
| Recover earlier intent and rationale                | `contextory_search` with a focused `query`, `mode` and `limit`; inspect full records with `contextory_entity_get`, including a cited `revision` when checking history. Verify current state before relying on an old decision.                                         |
| Continue a bounded result                           | `contextory_entity_get` uses `offset`/`limit` for children, job results and 400-character artifact pages. `contextory_history_get` uses the returned `nextBefore` as `before`. Flow pages/expansion use `contextory_flow_expand` with the original graph/snapshot IDs. |

For example, a task lookup can use `{"query":"How do provider connections install skills?","paths":["src/providers"],"budgetTokens":2000}`. Follow it with impact on the cited definition and inspect its current file and relevant callers. Avoid assuming this example's paths exist in another project.

Source tools accept file paths, unique names or `source:path#qualifiedName` where their schemas permit. Choose a path-qualified candidate when a name is ambiguous. A failed search or absent bounded path does not prove two components are independent. Inspect category, evidence locations and provenance for each material edge. Semantic unavailability has an explicit lexical fallback in hybrid search; semantic-only search may fail. Narrow query/path scope or page results when truncated instead of presenting a bounded slice as exhaustive.

## Freshness and coverage

Saved file create/edit/delete/rename, Git changes and configuration changes trigger debounced refresh, backed by polling. Task context, impact and path queries also verify disk content before answering. Re-query after relevant saves; do not request a full manual reindex after every edit. Source context describes saved files. Only trusted editor flow requests can carry unsaved overlays; their snapshots are separate and expire when documents change.

For an empty/stale/failed index, inspect status/errors and use `contextory_code_index_refresh` when a retry can help. For partial coverage, inspect the actual gaps: file/byte bounds may call for narrower reviewed configuration, while dynamic dispatch, callbacks and external code require native inspection. Repeated refresh does not create missing language support or execution evidence.

Native extraction covers TS/JS through its compiler and Python through isolated AST parsing. Markdown links and recognized configuration paths add explicit connections. Graphify JSON adds other language facts with supplied provenance. Changed cited source invalidates imported facts: regenerate the export and re-import using `contextory_code_index_refresh` with a workspace-relative `graphifyPath`; refresh alone cannot regenerate external analysis. Static calls, inferred message links and test references do not prove execution or coverage.

`contextory.project.json` holds reviewed configuration: schemaVersion 1, optional name, include/exclude patterns, entryPoints, conventions, maxFiles and maxBytes. Generated topology lives in rebuildable local storage; it does not approve requirements or overwrite authoritative work records. Consult user instructions and current decisions before treating a discovered convention as a constraint.

## Reference codebases

### Active workspace projects

Trusted local multi-root workspaces attach up to sixteen independent folder services. `contextory_workspace_get` lists public project IDs, names and canonical roots, plus attached workspace contexts; it never returns credential paths. All tools accept `projectId` and `workspaceId` as common scope. Selection applies only to that call. Omitting projectId/current stays on the server's project, regardless of the editor's selected project or earlier calls. Multiple attached editor contexts require workspaceId for cross-project operations. Unknown, detached or identity-changed projects fail; do not retry against a different project. Use the same projectId when reading returned record IDs, artifacts or graph pages. Keep the returned project identity with relative source paths and symbols. Read-only lookups never merge project memory.

The editor project selector scopes Requests, Knowledge, History, Versions, Architecture, checks and source navigation together; requests and specs carry project badges. Each folder retains its existing root-derived storage, ledger, graph, catalog, references, releases and checks. Removing a folder detaches its routing without deleting data. Shared/native hook observations stay with their observing project; usage is not inferred across project leases. A workspace is not a new merged project.

The CLI `projects [group-id] --descriptor <generic.json>` reads active membership or a coordinated request; `--project <id>` and `--workspace <id>` scope other CLI calls. A standalone service has only its local project until an editor attaches membership. Do not use codebaseId or a reference registration to authorize cross-project work. Coordinated requests use the workflow skill's project-owned branches.

When advertised, `contextory_codebase_list` returns the active workspace (`current`) and up to eight named local references. Register only a directory within the user's requested scope using `contextory_codebase_change` with `action:"add"`, an absolute `root`, optional `name`, and a new `operationId`. Registration resolves aliases and persists in the current service storage; it does not modify the reference. Detach using `action:"remove"`, its `codebaseId` and a new operation ID. Cached projections remain rebuildable service data.

Pass that ID as `codebaseId` on architecture, code context, search, impact, path, index/import and flow trace/expand calls. Paths, Graphify input and source IDs resolve inside that reference. References cannot use current-project `specId` or workflow mutations. Omission or `current` always means the active workspace, even after another reference query. Separate requests can analyze different references concurrently; there is no global project switch or inferred cross-repository relationship. Preserve each response's `codebase`, snapshot, coverage and citations when combining an explanation. A same-path/same-name symbol in two repositories is not the same source.

Reference context/impact/path/search and default architecture queries verify saved files on demand. References are not watched in the background. `refresh:false` explicitly uses cached architecture; use the default refresh after edits, and regenerate/re-import stale Graphify facts within the selected reference. Source files are parsed without executing them. Existing include/exclude/configuration and language coverage rules apply separately to each root. Reference search uses lexical graph matching (hybrid reports fallback); semantic-only reference search is unavailable. No active-project decisions, requirements, checks or unsaved editor overlays are imported into reference analysis.

CLI equivalents are `references`, `reference-add <folder> [--name <label>]`, `reference-remove <id>`, and source commands with `--codebase <id>`. Always keep `--root`/storage/descriptor on the current project whose reference registry you intend to use. Architecture in the editor offers **Add reference**, a **Codebase** selector and **Detach reference**; source navigation stays inside the selected root. Applying any learned behavior to the current application remains a separate user-authorized implementation task.

## Clients without a capability

Use only the tools advertised in the current session. After an extension upgrade, an existing connection may still expose older tools until the client reloads its MCP connection. Continue useful work with available search/flow tools, the packaged CLI, or native `rg`/file reads; state the missing graph coverage when it affects conclusions. Hooks are advisory and optional.

Run `node <installation>/dist/contextory.mjs help` for current CLI inputs. `context`, `impact`, `path`, `architecture` and `index` return JSON; `mcp` starts a hook-free stdio server. Supply the intended `--root` and either the existing service `--descriptor` or deliberately chosen `--storage` so the client reads the intended workspace and ledger. CLI code lookups do not replace MCP workflow mutations. Preserve the user's task and the host's permissions.

## Application definitions and documentation

Use `contextory_catalog_get` for file purposes, rules/features, UI placement/interactions, declared tests, pending proposals and source freshness. Record/proposal/inventory cursors are independent; keep paging each until exhausted. `contextory_project_export` overview enumerates stored documentation datasets; page current records, immutable revisions, history, relationships, source facts, jobs, usage metadata and artifacts with `offset`/`limit`. Keep sequence/snapshot and observed/approved/retired state. Use exact revisions for historical docs and current source for current behavior. The export grants no approval and exposes no service credentials or native conversations. Large result envelopes are read with `contextory_entity_get`.

| Python 3.10+ (optional) | Parses Python source and source flow |

Check installed runtimes

```powershell
node --version
python --version
```

## Install the VSIX

1. Download contextory-workspace-0.11.0.vsix and its .sha256 from the v0.11.0 GitHub release.
2. Compare the package SHA-256 with the accompanying checksum.
3. In Extensions, open the … menu, select Install from VSIX… and choose the downloaded file. Reload if prompted.
4. Open a trusted local project. The service and configured startup agents prepare in the background; open Contextory whenever you want to inspect work. The initial project has no requests.

[Download version 0.11.0](https://github.com/igormicadei/Contextory/releases/tag/v0.11.0)

Verify and install the release package

```powershell
(Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 .\contextory-workspace-0.11.0.vsix).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
Get-Content .\contextory-workspace-0.11.0.sha256
code --install-extension .\contextory-workspace-0.11.0.vsix
```

End users do not need npm, Rust, a database server or an embedding model. Install and sign in to the native agent through its own interface. Restart the editor after installing Node if its PATH has not refreshed.

## Upgrade, disconnect or uninstall

- To upgrade the same extension identity, install the newer VSIX, reload the editor and reload the native MCP session. Existing project records stay in editor-managed storage.
- To remove a bridge, click its green footer control or run Contextory: Disconnect an Agent. Only owned entries are removed. Use the command for a configured bridge whose light is gray.
- Before uninstalling, disconnect agents and back up the project ledger. Uninstall through Extensions; remove storage only after retaining the records you need.

## Configure one meaningful check

Open Preferences: Open Workspace Settings (JSON). Add a recipe for an existing project command. The example suits a project that uses Node’s built-in test runner; adapt its executable, arguments and timeout to your project.

}

# Daily user guide

## Multiple projects in one workspace

Open up to 16 trusted local, non-nested folders. The Project selector scopes Requests, Approvals, Knowledge, History, Versions and Architecture. Records, checks, evidence, source graphs, reference repositories and releases belong to each project independently. Removing a folder detaches it while retaining its storage.

1. In New request, select every affected project. Each selected project receives its own linked local request.
2. Inspect Across projects for branch status. Each branch needs its own milestones, specs, lease, checks and completed outcome.
3. If creation partially succeeds, use Retry missing branches on the original owner. Retain the original operation ID and inputs in agent automation. Missing or offline branches keep the group incomplete.

![Request list beside the selected specification.](../assets/panel-requests.png)

Requests in a horizontal editor Panel.

## Prepare connections at startup

Service startup and native bridge preparation run when the extension activates, even while Explorer or another sidebar is visible. Trust, folder, installed-agent and repaired runtime changes enter the same recovery path. Auto-connect pauses remain respected.

Auto-connect defaults to on and contextory.startupAgent defaults to auto, preparing all detected supported agents. Use the footer Auto-connect switch to pause automatic setup. Existing connections, sessions and records remain available. A manually disconnected provider stays opted out until reconnected.

Startup choices are auto, last-used, codex, claude, bob and none. Contextory prepares workspace-local configuration; native clients control trust, MCP reload, sign-in and session startup.

![Contextory sidebar with request progress and native agent controls.](../assets/companion-sidebar.png)

Contextory sidebar captured from the application; records are examples.

## Configure checks

Example workspace recipe

```json
{
  "contextory.checks": [{
    "id": "unit", "name": "Unit tests",
    "executable": "node", "args": ["--test"], "timeoutMs": 120000
  }]
}
```

Use executable plus argument arrays for real project checks. The agent invokes a configured recipe, polls its job and maps independently produced evidence to each current criterion. Source, contract or attempt changes can invalidate older evidence.

Configure up to 256 recipes. Invalid settings show Fix check settings while keeping the service connection and last valid recipe list. A fresh service has no valid recipes until configuration succeeds.

## Read model and usage records

The Usage section in Specification details and contextory_usage_get show observed metadata. Codex can report per-request token counts, Claude provides model metadata, and Bob’s documented hooks currently supply neither. Missing counts remain unavailable. Session/lease correlation is exact; unassigned observations remain unassigned.

Counts are not billing or quota estimates. Cached and reasoning tokens are subsets. Contextory does not read or mirror native conversations to calculate usage.

## Recover a connection or existing chat

1. Keep the project editor open and run Contextory: Check Native Connections. Read current-service MCP and hook observations in Output > Contextory.
2. Ask the existing agent to rediscover its advertised tools and make a read-only workspace/context call. If tools are missing, use Contextory: Restart Agent Extensions and reopen the chat as needed.
3. For missing or stale hooks, use Rebuild hooks in the footer or Contextory: Rebuild Agent Hooks. Select the project/provider, inspect repaired files and review native hook trust.
4. After one unchanged repair, inspect native trust and service logs. Repeating repairs cannot approve hooks. On Codex, /hooks approvals can differ for C: and c: path casing.

The proxy keeps discovery available during delayed startup and retries readiness for up to five minutes, with foreground waits bounded to 15 seconds. It rereads descriptors after restarts and never automatically replays a dispatched mutation. A contract mismatch needs the displayed reload/restart action.

## Project explanations

Use Tools > Documentation to find explanations linked to current source and tracked work. The bundled documentation/Carbon capability requires no external plugin; generation runs on demand.

[Read the project documentation guide](documentation.md)

## Follow the VS Code display language

Contextory follows the editor's display language for built-in labels, command titles, settings descriptions, native dialogs and webview controls. English and Brazilian Portuguese are supported. pt/pt-br select pt-BR; other unsupported locales fall back to English. The sidebar, horizontal panel, architecture, source flow and relationships share the same locale, including accessibility labels and dates.

1. Use VS Code's Configure Display Language command and choose English or Brazilian Portuguese. Install the language pack through VS Code if needed, then restart as requested by the editor.
2. Open Contextory. New webview documents take vscode.env.language, and the editor configures that normalized language for every connected project.
3. Ask the agent to read contextory_context_get. uiLanguage and contentLanguageInstruction tell it to write every new UI-facing record in the editor language, even when the conversation uses another language.

Existing requests, definitions, decisions, reports and source identifiers keep their original text. Localization translates source-owned interface messages before dynamic values are inserted; it never rewrites stored prose, code, paths, IDs or tool keys. Raw code/command output and unknown diagnostics retain their original language. Change language in VS Code and reload; Contextory has no competing language preference.

![Portuguese Contextory interface around original English project entries](../assets/knowledge-pt-BR.png)

Built-in controls follow Brazilian Portuguese; stored sample definitions remain exactly as authored.

The project's language is set only through authenticated editor configuration and persists in that project's service storage. Standalone/headless projects default to English; attaching to an editor-managed ledger retains its last configured language. Native hooks repeat the content-language instruction after session starts and before tools, including pending-review responses. This is an instruction to the native agent, not a language detector or automatic translation of its output.

# Code intelligence and advanced workflows

## Retrieve current task context

1. Start with contextory_workspace_get, then pass the intended projectId on every related call. UI selection never changes an agent server’s local default.
2. Call contextory_code_context_get with the actual task, known paths and a bounded budgetTokens value. Read the cited current source.
3. Use architecture for orientation, impact for dependencies/callers, path for connections, and flow trace for detailed calls/branches. Use search for earlier decisions and inspect their current state and revision.
4. Re-query relevant source after saved changes. Saved-file graphs refresh automatically; unsaved editor flow overlays remain separate. Page or narrow truncated results.

![Subsystem map, repository explorer and source inspector.](../assets/architecture-explorer.png)

Architecture explorer captured from Contextory.

Task-context arguments; replace the project ID

```json
{ "projectId": "PROJECT-ID", "query": "How are retries bounded?", "paths": ["src"], "budgetTokens": 3000 }
```

Qualify ambiguous definitions as source:path#qualifiedName. Task context accepts 512–6000 estimated tokens and caps JSON UTF-8 bytes at three times the estimate. Graph links and test references do not establish observed execution or complete behavioral coverage.

## Compare a reference repository

1. In Architecture, choose Add reference and select an authorized absolute local directory. Up to eight references can be registered per project.
2. Choose that Codebase, or pass its returned codebaseId on source/flow calls. Keep its identity and root with every citation.
3. Detach reference removes the registration while preserving source files. Registration and inspection do not authorize implementation in either repository.

Inspect an explicitly chosen reference

```powershell
node dist/contextory.mjs reference-add C:/Sources/LegacyApp --root C:/Projects/NewApp --name "Legacy app"
node dist/contextory.mjs references --root C:/Projects/NewApp
node dist/contextory.mjs architecture --root C:/Projects/NewApp --codebase ref-ID
```

# Governed project knowledge

## Describe intended application behavior

| Category | Required content |
| --- | --- |
| File | One source file and its responsibility |
| Rule | Invariant or condition; source and tests, or an explicit testGap |
| Feature | Observable capability; source and tests, or an explicit testGap |
| UI | Location, element, trigger, behavior and states; sources and tests or testGap |

Read contextory_catalog_get before related changes and page definitions, proposals and inventory independently. Generated entries begin as observations. A source graph describes possible relationships; it cannot approve a rule or infer intended interface behavior.

## Review pending items in Approvals

The persistent review alert, Approvals count and editor badge count pending change proposals only. Optional baseline review is collapsed initially; expand its summary with a click or keyboard to inspect observations. The chosen state is retained across refresh and navigation. These observations do not block work.

1. Open Approvals and read the agent’s explanation: what changes, why your approval is needed and how application behavior changes. Knowledge remains the browser for definitions, source coverage and immutable history.
2. Choose Approve or Reject without entering a comment. To ask for an update first, write your instructions and choose Request changes. A proposal with requested changes still blocks implementation; the agent revises that same proposal and waits for another decision.
3. Readable source snapshots refresh automatically and never grant approval or change the authored definition. Prior source hashes remain in history. Missing files still block approval. An edit during review refreshes the snapshot and asks you to inspect the latest item before retrying; no refresh button or refresh comment is required.

Saving, errors and success appear beside the controls. Failed responses preserve your instructions, and duplicate submissions are disabled. Switching to Knowledge and back preserves the draft; Knowledge filters do not hide approvals. Technical before/after definitions remain available through Definition history rather than filling the review card.

![Approvals showing the agent explanation, simple decisions and update instructions.](../assets/knowledge-preview.png)

Approvals rendered by the production webview with isolated example records; no real project approval was performed.

Human review in Approvals approves exact process/outcome changes and optional baselines. Agents use the leased auto-approval path for implementation maintenance/conflicts and cannot borrow human credentials. Pending proposals and stale affected approved definitions block completion. A compatible source refresh preserves the original human review and approved behavioral text; a changed file hash alone does not require changing the contract.

## Browse Knowledge independently

1. Choose Tools > Knowledge to browse current and historical definitions, their source/test links and history.
2. Expand Find definitions & coverage, then filter by text, path or category. File inventory stays available in this browser.
3. Choose Approvals to review pending items. Knowledge filters and pagination do not affect that queue; reviewed items disappear from Approvals and remain discoverable in Knowledge.

![Project knowledge browsing without approval forms.](../assets/knowledge-browser.png)

Knowledge browser using production UI and isolated fixture records.

## Bootstrap an existing project

Use the portable contextory-migrate skill within an authorized implementation request. contextory_catalog_migrate captures a bounded manifest and resumes by migrationId/cursor. Repeating the same operation/input returns the stored result. state=scanned means the file scan ended; it does not mean semantic review or approval is complete.

Inspect candidates against current source, callers, tests and historical decisions. Preserve contradictions, missing tests and unsupported runtime observations as explicit gaps. Reconcile files added after the captured manifest.

## Export stored documentation datasets

Discover and page project exports

```json
{ "section": "overview", "offset": 0, "limit": 20 }
```

Call contextory_project_export with the selected projectId. Page records, revisions, history, relationships, code_files, code_nodes, code_edges, code_imports, jobs, usage and artifacts until nextOffset=null. Keep sequence/snapshot, current versus historical state, provenance and source freshness. Artifacts use 400-character units; other datasets page rows.

This export excludes credentials, native conversations and numeric embedding vectors. Large responses may return artifact handles for further paging. A read-only export needs no implementation request.

## Choose approval by behavioral impact

Compatible maintenance needs no new human decision. Agents may auto-approve implementation conflicts too, with an explicit conflict assessment, rationale, source/test links and validation. Conflicts involving process rules or results, changed approved behavior, retirements and uncertain conflicts require human review before implementation. New observations have optional baseline review and do not trigger mandatory approval alerts.

Compatible source maintenance under the current lease

```json
{
  "action": "revise",
  "id": "KN-existing",
  "expectedRevision": 2,
  "specId": "SPEC-current",
  "leaseId": "current-lease",
  "operationId": "unique-operation-id",
  "compatibility": "preserved",
  "impact": "implementation",
  "autoApprove": true,
  "content": {
    "category": "feature",
    "title": "Stable greeting",
    "description": "Returns the configured greeting.",
    "sources": [
      {
        "path": "src/greeting.ts",
        "symbol": "greet"
      }
    ],
    "tests": [
      {
        "path": "tests/greeting.test.ts"
      }
    ]
  },
  "reason": "Function A replaced by B with the same results, errors and side effects; record the relevant validation."
}
```

Use compatibility=conflicting and impact=implementation only when the conflict cannot affect process rules or results. Preserve approved behavior descriptions and UI contracts exactly; file-purpose prose may be corrected for implementation changes. The server declines auto-approval for changed approved behavior, rule conflicts and process/outcome or unclassified related decisions. decisionIds retains links to earlier decisions. Auto-approval is an agent assessment, not proof of semantic equivalence or passing tests.

Every revision preserves the original definition, before/after source fingerprints, target revision, reason, spec, actor and review mode. Auto-approved changes have state=auto_approved; observed targets remain observed and approved behavioral targets retain their original human review. Knowledge displays agent maintenance provenance, and history, search, reports and project export retain the change. Test references never substitute for independent executed evidence.

Auto-approval preserves behavioral descriptions and UI contracts even on observed entries. When an approved file-purpose description changes, the new file observation is not attributed to the earlier human review; its approved baseline revision remains traceable.

## Wait before implementing a disputed change

Prepare the concrete proposal before editing disputed behavior. PreToolUse denies implementation tools while any project proposal is pending; Stop blocks completion. Read-only tools, catalog preparation, configured checks, questions/wait and lease renewal remain available. Contextory also rejects workflow mutations through its service, so direct MCP calls do not bypass the gate. Do not busy-poll or use another shell to proceed. Approval status is re-read on each event and survives service restarts; silence and timeout never approve anything.

Codex/Claude launchers emit structured deny/block responses plus exit code 2; Bob uses blocking stderr/exit code 2. A failed or obsolete approval-status contract blocks implementation/completion until recovery. Reload the service and native hook runtime together after upgrading. Native trust and actual hook delivery remain host-owned. Generic MCP has no native file-tool hook: the service enforces its own workflow, while agents must honor the wait for external edits. Hooks cannot intercept unreported changes, a human editor, or a client that never invokes them.

After approval, implement and validate the accepted behavior. After rejection, retain or restore the established behavior and validate it. Superseding process/outcome or unclassified decisions requires a human-approved proposal in the current spec, with the old decision in decisionIds and the exact replacement choice as content.description; pass its approvalId to contextory_decision_record. Only implementation-to-implementation decision conflicts auto-review.

## Trace a regression to a recorded change

1. Recover the affected feature/rule/UI contract, current source and last known working check or version. Record the symptom and reproducer as a finding.
2. Follow impact/path relationships and search by feature, path/symbol, catalog ID and earlier decisions. Page history and inspect exact before/after revisions, hashes, agent or human review, spec and evidence, including auto-approved changes.
3. Compare actual Git membership and the last working source. Reproduce candidate causes; static edges and recording intervals do not prove causation or shipped inclusion. Use a focused regression check and Git history/bisect when useful.
4. Link the confirmed finding/fix to the responsible change/spec/source with contextory_relationship_change. Record uncertainty if the cause is unproven; update catalog/docs and submit current independent evidence.

Auto-approval reduces interruptions, not traceability. All material changes still require indexed explanations and validation evidence so a later agent can investigate what changed and why.

## Return to the originating conversation

Attach the exact native session ID supplied by the Contextory hook. The project, provider, session and specification are saved on proposals and retained on claimed work after lease release. Approval, rejection and feedback are durable audit events returned only to that exact provider/session in the same project. An unknown origin remains unbound; the extension never guesses the active chat.

A trusted PreToolUse or Stop hook can wait up to four minutes for your decision and return it to that conversation. Approval releases the approved operation; rejection prevents the waiting operation, and feedback asks for a revised proposal. Expiry or service failure keeps the operation blocked. Responses remain queued until a matching hook receives them; transport acknowledgement does not prove the model acted on them. Hooks that are not trusted or a fully stopped client cannot resume automatically.

Use Reopen conversation on an approval or a specification’s Contract tab. Claude opens the saved session through the installed native extension command. Codex resumes that exact saved conversation in an interactive terminal with codex resume, because its documented extension commands expose neither targeted reopening nor targeted message submission. Bob, generic clients or an unavailable Claude command copy the saved session ID for manual history recovery. The native client owns history availability and permissions; no response is injected into an arbitrary chat.

[Claude session recovery contract](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/vs-code#launch-a-vs-code-tab-from-other-tools)

# Project documentation

## Find an explanation

Contextory includes project documentation as an optional capability. The software-documentation 1.0.1 runtime, its authoring/update/source-comment/integration playbooks and the complete Carbon 1.0.0 module ship in the extension and CLI. Local fonts, tokens, templates and references need no separate plugin installation. Reading explanations works without Python; generation uses Python 3.11+ configured by contextory.pythonExecutable.

1. Choose Tools > Documentation. Search for a feature or behavior, optionally filter by source path, and choose English or Portuguese.
2. Read the explanation, stable page/section ID, source links and freshness badge. A draft, an unknown baseline and a stale explanation still need review; documentation never grants approval to a requirement.
3. From Architecture, choose Explain this area for the current source scope. In a request, expand Brief & actions and choose Related documentation to find sections linked to the request or its descendant records. Reference codebases remain a separate read-only source scope.

![Documentation search, English and Portuguese selection, stale explanation and source/record links.](../assets/documentation-browser.png)

Production documentation browser with isolated fixture explanations and explicit stale-source state.

## Author and build with your agent

1. Ask the agent to use contextory-documentation. It reads current source, catalog and the relevant exported Contextory datasets with their project identity and approval/history provenance.
2. Map the project and author substantive paired English/pt-BR explanations in .documentation/project.json. The bundled init operation creates a draft, not finished documentation. Preserve existing content, translations, IDs, URLs and assets.
3. Use contextory_docs_run for map/init/validate/build/integrations/migrate/readme/Pages operations and poll the returned job. Generation runs on demand and cannot gate service startup. Mutating operations require the agent’s current specification lease.
4. Review the generated responsive Carbon site, both locales, local search, examples, native source comments and coverage gaps. Consumer bundles include their own read-only documentation MCP and installer. Do not claim complete behavior coverage from file counts or a passed build.

The generator creates schema 2 Carbon sites, and retrieval also reads schema 1. Migration previews by default, creates a backup on apply and leaves migrated content in draft for review. Contextory’s own schema-1 site build remains separately pinned; this feature does not upgrade that corpus.

## Connect explanations to changes

After comparing a section with current sources, the agent uses contextory_docs_link with its page/section IDs, current corpus fingerprint, local record IDs and a reason. Contextory retains citation hashes, record revisions, semantic fingerprints and an audit trail of before/after associations. It stores these observed links in the selected project’s ledger; it does not inject private ledger history into public HTML.

Changed text/citations, changed or missing cited files and meaningful changes to linked records mark a section stale. Lease renewal alone does not invalidate the explanation. Current-project code context includes bounded relevant explanations when its token budget permits. Source definitions, generated architecture, authored explanations, historical decisions and human-approved requirements retain different authority.

Expand Keep documentation current for source mapping or validation. A successful runtime job can return valid=false, shown as needs review. Large results are retained as JSON artifacts and can be paged through project export. Exact operation retries recover the same job; failed/interrupted mutations are never replayed automatically.

## Publish explicitly and verify

Implementing documentation does not publish a connected project. With publication authorization, inspect pages_plan, select the intended remote, then run pages_publish with publish=true and the current lease. Verify pages_status against the actual live artifact. The bundled upstream publisher preserves orphan gh-pages history and rejects foreign branch replacement. GitHub CLI authentication/network/Pages availability remain environmental requirements.

Missing Python affects generator jobs only. Configure its executable and start a new operation after inspecting any partial files. A failed or unavailable documentation corpus does not block source context or the service. Human approvals remain in Approvals, and references never grant writes into another project.

# Project versions and releases

## Inspect repository-wide version history

Versions belongs to the whole repository, independently of requests, specs and leases. While the service runs, it observes Git and records exact commit membership for releases and unreleased changes. Read contextory_version_get or the Versions view and page commits and semantic records separately. Local tag observation does not prove remote publication.

![Project versions and release details in the editor Panel.](../assets/panel-versions.png)

Versions captured from the application.

## Prepare, apply and publish separately

1. Prepare a concrete release plan: inspect proposed version, HEAD, changed version files and changelog. Preparation does not edit source.
2. With authorization for the release, apply the reviewed plan to create its version commit and annotated local tag. Resolve stale plans or unrelated dirty changes before applying.
3. Publish the exact tag as a separate action using the configured Git remote and authentication. Verify remote state. Local application alone does not publish extension packages, releases or the documentation site.
4. After an uncertain result, recover the owned operation with its original operation ID/input. Never force or replace an existing tag. Cancel only an untouched plan.

Inspect and prepare; use returned IDs/revisions for later actions

```powershell
node dist/contextory.mjs versions
node dist/contextory.mjs release-prepare minor --operation prepare-unique-id
node dist/contextory.mjs versions REL-ID --offset 0 --limit 20
```

> Implementing software or rewriting documentation does not authorize releasing the repository. Release publication and a live editor installation remain separate user actions.

## Configure version adapters

contextory.release.json supports schemaVersion, initialVersion, tagPrefix, remote, optional branch, changelogPath and versionFiles. JSON adapters select key paths; text adapters use bounded prefix/suffix replacements. Use repository-relative ordinary files. Plans bind the exact source/configuration state and preserve unrelated changes.

Semantic records associated between release cutoffs remain interval associations, not proof they shipped in a commit. Release revisions and history remain exportable.

Native hooks enforce pending approval decisions before implementation and Stop, in addition to lifecycle reminders and normalized metadata. 1. Run Contextory: Export Generic MCP Connection in the selected project.
2. Import its server entry into your client and copy the exported codebase, workflow and migration skill folders into that client’s supported discovery location.
3. Approve/reload through that client and make a read-only workspace/context call. .contextory/skills is an export location, not universal automatic discovery.

Contextory sidebar captured from the application; records are examples.

node dist/contextory.mjs context "payment retries" --root C:/Projects/Checkout --budget 3000

# Limits and compatibility

## Supported and unqualified environments

The qualified preview uses Windows, trusted local folders, Node.js 24+, VS Code 1.96+ or IBM Bob, and at most 16 non-nested workspace projects. Remote/virtual workspaces, other operating systems, arbitrary monorepo scale and authenticated end-to-end conversations in every native agent are not qualified.

## Source and flow analysis boundaries

Default interactive flow uses five call hops, 150 nodes, 300 edges and a two-second budget. Python flow scanning is bounded to 500 files, 512 KiB per file and 12 MiB total. Frontiers, cycles, unresolved targets and size/time boundaries remain visible. Expand or retrace to continue.

TypeScript and Python extraction is static. Dynamic dispatch, generated code, external dependencies and framework runtime behavior may not resolve. Other flow languages rely on available editor call hierarchy and do not automatically receive branch extraction. Saved graph results and unsaved flow overlays have different freshness rules.

## Recovery, revisions and concurrency

One active implementation lease owns each specification. Reread a record after a revision conflict; do not retry changed input with an old operation ID. Reuse exact operation/input only after an uncertain result. Cross-project creation is recoverable and may partially succeed; it is not an atomic transaction.

An unavailable source, stale Graphify import, missing independent check, pending Knowledge proposal or unresolved blocking finding stays an explicit limitation or completion blocker. Native permissions remain in force.

# Runtime architecture

## Follow the process boundaries

| Component | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Native agent | Conversation, model, sign-in, editing and native permissions |
| Editor extension and webviews | Trusted workspace setup, UI, source navigation and live theme integration |
| Isolated Node service | Role-scoped tools, workflow enforcement, ledger, search, checks and release observation |
| Analysis workers / Python parser | Bounded static extraction outside the Extension Host; no workspace module imports |
| SQLite storage | Authoritative records/revisions/artifacts and rebuildable graph/search projections |

Native MCP proxies connect to private local service descriptors. Hooks provide bounded lifecycle reminders and normalized metadata. Native/headless MCP, briefs and hooks share runtime guidance; provider-specific configuration remains in explicit adapters.

Native hooks enforce pending approval decisions before implementation and Stop, in addition to lifecycle reminders and normalized metadata. Agents may auto-approve only implementation maintenance/conflicts; process/outcome conflicts wait for human Approvals. Enforcement requires the host to trust and invoke the updated hooks.

## Preserve authoritative records

Requests, contracts, immutable revisions, decisions, check evidence, outcomes, Knowledge definitions and release records are authoritative project history. The source graph and lexical/vector indexes are projections that can be rebuilt. Rebuilding source analysis must not erase workflow history.

Each workspace project owns its ledger, sessions, leases, checks, references and releases. Cross-project routing validates current editor membership and preserves the caller’s role. A reference repository has an isolated read-only projection inside its owning project.

## Understand privacy and authority

Contextory stores concise project explanations and observed metadata rather than native chat transcripts. Check output and indexed project content are retained locally. Human Knowledge review is enforced by service roles, but a process with unrestricted local filesystem access is not isolated from service credentials or SQLite by this design.

The bilingual corpus is the source of the human pages, Markdown and LLM exports.
