title: Frequently asked questions
text:
# Frequently asked questions

## Does Contextory replace my chat or model?

No. Keep using your native agent. Contextory supplies shared project records and tools; conversation history, sign-in, model selection and editing stay with the client.

## Do I need Python or a model download?

Node.js 24+ is required. Python 3.10+ is needed only for Python analysis. Local semantic retrieval is optional; lexical/structural retrieval works without an embedding download.

## Does a code question need a tracked request?

Read-only source questions and documentation exports do not. Authorized implementation uses requests, milestones, criteria, a session/lease and independent evidence before explicit completion.

## Why is a submitted specification still open?

Outcome submission records the explanation. The agent must separately request completion with the returned current revision. Missing checks, stale evidence, dependencies, blocking findings and catalog proposals can prevent completion.

## Does a green agent light prove authentication?

It proves observed MCP traffic for that configured provider in this service instance. It does not prove model sign-in or execution of every hook. Use native trust controls and connection diagnostics for more detail.

## Can an agent approve its own Knowledge definition?

Compatible maintenance needs no new human decision. Agents may auto-approve implementation conflicts too, with an explicit conflict assessment, rationale, source/test links and validation. Conflicts involving process rules or results, changed approved behavior, retirements and uncertain conflicts require human review before implementation. New observations have optional baseline review and do not trigger mandatory approval alerts.

## Is a graph or linked test execution evidence?

No. Static extraction and test references indicate possible relationships. Verification requires actual current check results with their provenance and source/contract/attempt fingerprints.

## Does Contextory follow VS Code's language?

Yes. The built-in interface supports English and Brazilian Portuguese using vscode.env.language, with English fallback for other locales. Agents receive the project uiLanguage and must author new interface entries in that language. Historical/user content and code are preserved; documentation retains its English/pt-BR pair.

title: Troubleshooting and recovery
text:
# Troubleshooting and recovery

## Recover service and native connections

| Symptom | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Service unavailable | Keep the project editor open, check Node 24+ in its PATH, set contextory.nodeExecutable if needed and inspect Output > Contextory |
| Analysis or connection disabled | Trust a supported local workspace; avoid virtual/remote or nested project roots |
| Gray agent light | Hover for configuration/traffic state, click to retry setup, review native MCP/hook trust and make a read-only call |
| Tools missing in an old chat | Restart agent extensions, reload the native MCP connection and reopen the chat as required by that client |
| Hooks remain unobserved | Rebuild once, inspect repaired files, then check native trust and trigger a supported lifecycle event; unchanged files are not execution evidence |
| Unowned or malformed configuration | Resolve the concrete conflict; registration preserves unowned entries and refuses linked paths |
| Older service after an upgrade | Follow the mismatch message; close project editors for about 65 seconds before reopening when requested |

[Connection and hook recovery walkthrough](user-guide.md)

## Automatic recovery and request timeouts

The editor probes service health every 20 seconds with a five-second timeout. Lost streams, including clean closure, trigger reconnection after 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and at most 30 seconds. The view labels retained data and offers Retry now. Recovery never replays failed mutations.

REQUEST_TIMEOUT means an operation exceeded its request budget; it does not establish SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE. Ordinary tools allow 120 seconds and release operations have their separate five-minute budget. For an uncertain mutation response, recover with the exact original operation ID and input.

For the former Configure at most 30 check recipes error, upgrade to 0.8.0: up to 256 recipes are supported. Fix duplicate IDs or malformed recipes through Fix check settings. Configuration errors retain the service and its last valid recipes.

Rebuild hooks writes managed files immediately. Changed repairs follow contextory.restartAfterSetup: prompt, automatic or never. The installed Codex extension exposes no public hook-refresh command; Contextory cannot grant native trust or guarantee immediate reload inside a running chat. Review /hooks in that session, keep workspace path casing consistent and reopen the chat after restarting extensions when required.

## Recover source results and completion

| Symptom | Action |
| --- | --- |
| An item remains pending in Approvals | Read the inline error. Sources refresh automatically; no comment is needed. Restore missing files or ask the agent to correct references. Request changes for an outdated target or incomplete explanation; the agent revises the proposal and waits again. If a reply is queued, resume the linked conversation and check native hook trust. |
| Python flow fails | Check Python 3.10+ and contextory.pythonExecutable; use an absolute executable path if needed |
| Unexpected source root | Set projectId/codebaseId explicitly and focus the intended editor symbol before tracing |
| Source search seems stale | Re-query saved source; refresh an empty/failed index, inspect exclusions and regenerate/re-import stale Graphify data |
| Semantic search unavailable | Prepare the optional local runtime and index, or use lexical/hybrid fallback |
| Spec stays submitted | Poll check jobs, resolve blockers and stale evidence, submit every criterion mapping, then explicitly complete using the returned revision |
| Cross-project group incomplete | Restore missing/offline workspace members and recover missing branches on the original owner; verify each local request |

## Report a reproducible issue

Include Contextory version, editor/version, Node/Python versions, exact error text and reproduction steps. Remove credentials, private descriptors, tokens and project-private records before sharing logs. Preserve current coverage and unverified limits.

[Open the issue tracker](https://github.com/igormicadei/Contextory/issues)

title: Write useful implementation outcomes
text:
# Write useful implementation outcomes

## Explain what changed and why

- Identify the request/spec, current revision and original user intent. Describe the resulting behavior with source references.
- Record findings with impact, resolution and why the fix works. Explicitly say when there were no findings.
- Explain material choices, alternatives and consequences. Distinguish an agent decision from a human requirement.
- Map every current criterion exactly once to current evidence. Retain actual command/job result, origin, skips and limits.
- Include catalog.recordIds and catalog.explanation when the catalog exists. Explain updated definitions or unchanged behavior.

## Submit and explicitly complete

1. Finish source/configuration edits before final independent checks. Later changes can invalidate evidence.
2. Submit contextory_outcome_submit with the current revision, evidence mappings, report/changelog text and limitations.
3. Use contextory_spec_change action=complete with the returned revision and a new operationId. Confirm state=completed and export the request report.

![Request list beside the selected specification.](../assets/panel-requests.png)

Requests in a horizontal editor Panel.

The snapshot hashes the complete contents of manifest files using 1 MiB read chunks. Files larger than 20 MiB remain included; fixtures do not need to be removed to run checks. If a file changes size, modification/metadata timestamps, identity or type during the read, capture is rejected with STALE_SOURCE. Before/after command snapshot comparison and independent-evidence requirements remain active.

# Validation and evidence boundaries

## Match each check to its claim

| Check | Establishes |
| --- | --- |
| npm run check | Skill bundle consistency, types, production build, backend and browser UI regression checks |
| Service/headless/registration integration | Tool contracts, transport, role isolation, setup ownership and tracked workflow scenarios |
| Editor-host smoke checks | Actual packaged activation, commands, service, configuration and persistence in isolated profiles |
| docs:validate and docs:build | Bilingual corpus structure, cited source hashes, images, generated exports and local links/anchors |
| Documentation browser review | Desktop/mobile layout, locale parity, navigation, search and screenshot rendering for the reviewed build |

## Separate earlier qualification from this rewrite

The original validation record and release notes are preserved as historical downloads. Their passing results describe the code/artifacts tested at that time. They are not automatically new test executions for this documentation rewrite. The rewrite’s concrete commands/results belong in .documentation/REVIEW.md.

Existing screenshots are application captures with example records. The documentation build validates file presence and bilingual captions/alt text. Browser review verifies rendering; it does not recreate an authenticated native-agent conversation.

## Keep remaining gaps explicit

The earlier documentation rewrite recorded an unavailable service; the 0.8.0 delivery recovered the original project ledger and uses tracked release checks. Catalog entries remain observations until human review. Native trust, authenticated agent chats, dynamic/static-analysis gaps, remote workspaces and other operating systems retain their own qualification limits.

## Approval policy and traceability validation

Disposable integration fixtures exercise compatible function replacement with the same result, approved-contract preservation, audited implementation conflicts, process/outcome/rule guards, exact decision supersession approval, source staleness, service-side bypass rejection, restart persistence and real packaged hook processes for Codex/Claude/Bob. Browser fixtures verify optional observations, required review counts and visible agent provenance. These tests establish launcher/service contracts; they do not automate authenticated native conversations, hook trust or interception of unreported edits.

## English and Portuguese localization checks

Checks cover locale normalization/fallback, static message and manifest coverage, substitution marker preservation, untouched dynamic records/code/attributes, webview language/CSP, project-scoped authenticated configuration, persisted context/hook instructions, English regressions and Portuguese navigation/accessibility/layout in sidebar, short panel and standalone workbenches. text:
# MCP API reference

## Read the advertised contract

Contextory 0.11.0 defines 39 tools. The following Zod schema excerpts were extracted with the TypeScript parser from the saved source without executing application code. They preserve required/optional/default/range semantics. The running MCP tools/list response is authoritative for the installed client version. contextory_catalog_review is human-UI-only even if its contract is visible.

Every tool additionally accepts optional projectId and workspaceId. Omitted/current project scope stays on that server’s project. Source tools additionally accept optional codebaseId where their schema/advertised contract permits it. Lines/characters in product tool source references are zero-based; documentation citation lines are one-based.

Shared schema aliases

```typescript
const id = z.string().min(1).max(160);
const text = z.string().min(1).max(12000);
const operationId = z.string().min(8).max(160);
const expectedRevision = z.number().int().positive().optional();
const source = z.object({
  path: z.string().min(1).max(2000),
  line: z.number().int().nonnegative().optional(),
  character: z.number().int().nonnegative().optional(),
  symbol: z.string().max(500).optional(),
});
const lease = { specId: id, leaseId: id };
const category = z.enum(["file", "rule", "feature", "ui"]);
export const catalogContent = z
  .object({
    category,
    title: z.string().trim().min(1).max(300),
    description: text,
    sources: z.array(source).min(1).max(30),
    tests: z.array(source).max(30).default([]),
    testGap: z.string().trim().min(1).max(2000).optional(),
    ui: z
      .object({
        location: text,
        element: text,
        trigger: text,
        behavior: text,
        states: text,
      })
      .optional(),
  })
  .superRefine((p, ctx) => {
    if (p.category === "file" && p.sources.length !== 1)
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: "custom",
        message: "A file entry describes exactly one source file.",
      });
    if (p.category === "ui" && !p.ui)
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: "custom",
        message:
          "UI contracts need location, element, trigger, behavior and states.",
      });
    if (p.category !== "file" && !p.tests.length && !p.testGap)
      ctx.addIssue({
        code: "custom",
        message: "Behavior needs test links or an explicit testGap.",
      });
  });
const limits = z
  .object({
    callDepth: z.number().int().min(0).max(12).optional(),
    nodes: z.number().int().min(5).max(500).optional(),
    edges: z.number().int().min(5).max(1000).optional(),
    targetsPerCall: z.number().int().min(1).max(30).optional(),
    timeoutMs: z.number().int().min(100).max(10000).optional(),
  })
  .optional();

```

## Revisions, retries and completion

Read a record before editing. Existing records require current expectedRevision. Use a fresh operationId (8–160 characters) for a new mutation; retry uncertain work only with its exact original input/ID. Implementation writes require the attached session’s active spec lease except documented setup/release operations. Native permissions still apply.

[Evidence and completion sequence](outcomes.md)

## Hooks rebuild

Repair one provider’s managed hooks; requires a reachable service and preserves native trust.

Input schema · src/contracts/tools.ts:129

```typescript
z.object({
      operationId,
      provider: z.enum(["codex", "claude", "bob"]),

```

## Workspace get

Discover project/workspace identities and optional coordinated-request status.

Input schema · src/contracts/tools.ts:137



## Version get

Read repository-wide version state, commits and semantic records with independent pagination.

Input schema · src/contracts/tools.ts:152

```typescript
z.object({
      releaseId: id.optional(),
      offset: z.number().int().nonnegative().default(0),

```

## Release prepare

Prepare a concrete release plan without source edits; no spec lease is needed.

Input schema · src/contracts/tools.ts:161

## Release change

Apply, publish, recover or cancel an authorized release plan using its current revision.

```typescript
      operationId,

      expectedRevision: z.number().int().positive(),

```

## Project export

Page stored datasets for documentation, retaining sequence, snapshots and provenance.

Input schema · src/contracts/tools.ts:180

```typescript
z.object({
      section: z
        .enum([
          "overview",
          "records",
          "revisions",
          "history",
          "relationships",
          "code_files",
          "code_nodes",
          "code_edges",
          "code_imports",
          "jobs",
          "usage",
          "artifacts",
        ])
        .default("overview"),
      entityId: id.optional(),
      artifact: z.string().min(1).max(200).optional(),
      offset: z.number().int().nonnegative().default(0),
      limit: z.number().int().min(1).max(50).default(20),

```

## Catalog get

Read catalog definitions, pending proposals, source freshness and optional file inventory.

Input schema · src/contracts/tools.ts:206

```typescript
z.object({
      category: category.optional(),
      path: z.string().max(2000).optional(),
      query: z.string().max(4000).optional(),
      inventory: z.boolean().default(false),
      pendingOnly: z.boolean().default(false),
      offset: z.number().int().nonnegative().default(0),
      limit: z.number().int().min(1).max(50).default(20),
    })
```

## Catalog change

Compatible maintenance needs no new human decision. Agents may auto-approve implementation conflicts too, with an explicit conflict assessment, rationale, source/test links and validation. Conflicts involving process rules or results, changed approved behavior, retirements and uncertain conflicts require human review before implementation. New observations have optional baseline review and do not trigger mandatory approval alerts.

Input schema · src/contracts/tools.ts:219

```typescript
z.object({
      operationId,
      ...lease,
      action: z.enum(["create", "revise", "retire"]),
      id: id.optional(),
      expectedRevision,
      content: catalogContent.optional(),
      reason: text.trim().min(1),
      migrationId: id.optional(),
      compatibility: z
        .enum(["preserved", "changed", "conflicting", "unknown"])
        .default("unknown"),
      impact: z
        .enum(["implementation", "process", "outcome", "unknown"])
        .default("unknown"),
      autoApprove: z.boolean().default(false),
      decisionIds: z.array(id).max(30).default([]),
      explanation: z
        .object({
          change: text.trim().min(1),
          approvalReason: text.trim().min(1),
          behavior: text.trim().min(1),
        })
        .optional(),
    })
```

## Catalog review

Human UI only. Approve/reject an exact revision without a required comment, or send feedback with update instructions. Source snapshots refresh automatically without approval. The legacy refresh action remains compatible. Requested changes keep implementation blocked until the agent revises the proposal and receives another decision.

Input schema · src/contracts/tools.ts:248

```typescript
z
      .object({
        operationId,
        id,
        expectedRevision: z.number().int().positive(),
        action: z.enum(["approve", "reject", "feedback", "refresh"]),
        reason: z.string().max(12000).trim().default(""),
      })
      .refine((p) => p.action !== "feedback" || p.reason.length > 0, {
        message: "Describe the update you want the agent to make.",
        path: ["reason"],
      })
```

## Catalog migrate

Bootstrap file descriptions in resumable batches; scanned candidates still need semantic review.

Input schema · src/contracts/tools.ts:264

```typescript
z.object({
      operationId,
      ...lease,
      migrationId: id.optional(),
      limit: z.number().int().min(1).max(50).default(20),
    })
```

## Context get

Read workspace contracts, active work, check recipes and guidance before implementation.

Input schema · src/contracts/tools.ts:274

```typescript
z.object({ specId: id.optional() })
```

The response includes uiLanguage (en or pt-BR) and contentLanguageInstruction from the editor-configured project. Use it for all newly authored UI-facing prose; preserve stored history and exact protocol/source identifiers. Standalone projects default to English unless an editor configured their ledger.

## Entity get

Read a current or immutable record revision, child page, job or artifact page.

Input schema · src/contracts/tools.ts:279

```typescript
z.object({
      id,
```

# Release v0.11.0

## Decide from a clear explanation

Approval cards ask the agent to explain what changes, why approval is needed and how application behavior changes. Approve or Reject needs no comment. Request changes accepts instructions, keeps implementation blocked and lets the agent update the same proposal before another decision. Historical before/after definitions, actors, hashes and rationale remain indexed.

Readable source snapshots refresh automatically without a user comment or implicit approval. Missing references, concurrent edits and changed targets remain protected. Optional baseline review starts collapsed and can be opened with a click or keyboard; its chosen state survives refresh and navigation. Pending approval decisions remain visible.

## Keep the originating conversation

The project, provider and exact native session are retained on linked work and proposals. Durable approval/rejection/feedback replies return only to that session through trusted hooks. A waiting hook can return the response within a four-minute budget; expiry or service failure never grants approval. Queued/offered/unbound status distinguishes transport from model execution.

Reopen conversation uses the installed Claude session command. Codex resumes the exact saved conversation in an interactive terminal and requires its CLI. Bob/generic clients or unavailable adapters copy the session ID for native history recovery. A stopped or untrusted client may need manual resume; unknown historical session identities are never guessed. Native permissions, sign-in and history availability stay with the client.

## Install and verify

Download contextory-workspace-0.11.0.vsix and the matching .sha256, compare the SHA-256, then use Extensions > Install from VSIX. Reload the editor and native integrations when prompted so the new tool contracts and waiting hooks are discovered. Review hook trust in the native client. English and Brazilian Portuguese follow the VS Code display language, including instructions for new agent-authored UI entries.

[Download the 0.11.0 release](https://github.com/igormicadei/Contextory/releases/tag/v0.11.0)

Qualification covers approval behavior and source history, live waiting-hook responses, service/headless/registration boundaries, English/Portuguese UI, keyboard collapse/recovery, bilingual documentation, canonical skill consistency and package checksums. Trusted local Windows workspaces with Node.js 24+ remain the qualified environment. Authenticated live model conversations retain their native-client limits.

# Release v0.10.0

## Selective approval with enforced waiting

Agents may auto-approve compatible maintenance and implementation conflicts with an explicit impact classification, reason, validation and audit record. Conflicts affecting process rules or outcomes, uncertain conflicts and retirements require human review before implementation. Native PreToolUse/Stop hooks and the service gate keep the agent waiting for that decision; silence or elapsed time never grants approval.

Definitions retain their before/after revisions, source hashes, actors, rationale, related decisions, specifications and check evidence. Use the catalog and history to investigate a feature that stopped working and connect a confirmed regression to its responsible change. Generated observations have optional review and do not become human-approved requirements.

## Follow the VS Code language

Controls and extension contributions use the VS Code display language: English or Brazilian Portuguese, with English fallback for other locales. The editor propagates uiLanguage and a content-language instruction to project context and hooks. Agents must write new UI-facing entries in that language, preserving exact identifiers, source code and historical text. Documentation retains both locales.

Compare the checksum before installing through Extensions > Install from VSIX, then reload the editor/native integrations when prompted. This delivery builds locally and pushes source commits; GitHub release asset publication and installation into an active editor are separate actions.

# Release v0.9.0

## Review pending knowledge in Approvals

Approvals is a primary destination beside Work and Requests, with a pending count. Alerts and Review now open the queue directly. It fetches observed baselines and pending proposals before pagination; Knowledge remains an independent browser for definitions, history and source coverage.

When sources changed, inspect them, enter a reason and refresh the source snapshot before approving the new revision. Refresh keeps the item pending. Inline errors explain missing/conflicting references; reasons survive navigation/failure and duplicate submissions are disabled. This does not grant agents human approval.

## Independent project explanations and Carbon

Tools > Documentation searches English/Portuguese explanations by topic, source path or tracked record. Architecture offers Explain this area; request actions find related documentation, including links on descendant specs. Current-project source context retrieves relevant excerpts even before a new specification has explicit associations.

The extension/CLI bundles software-documentation 1.0.1, its playbooks, the complete Carbon 1.0.0 module and local fonts/tokens/templates. No separate plugin is needed. Three Contextory tools provide reading/guidance/jobs, all upstream generator/consumer/Pages actions and audited observed associations. Text, source and meaningful record changes mark linked explanations stale.

Reading works without Python. Generation runs only on demand with Python 3.11+ and a current lease for writes; it never blocks service startup. Existing schema-1 corpora can be read, and migration previews/backups preserve authored content before schema-2 Carbon generation. Publishing a connected project remains an explicitly authorized action.

## Work console and reliable connections

Work and Requests focus the interface on the current specification and one request plan. Tools exposes project exploration on demand. The same view adapts to a narrow vertical sidebar and a wide horizontal panel while preserving selection, drafts and scroll.

Progress shows criterion evidence, running checks, blockers and latest work instead of a time estimate. Persistent review alerts, a view badge and deduplicated notifications expose Knowledge awaiting human review.

# Source retrieval skill

## Source retrieval skill

This is a portable agent instruction resource distributed unchanged to supported clients. The linked bilingual guide explains its task sequence, source freshness, permissions and limits. Read the installed SKILL.md and its linked references when actually applying the skill.

[Read the bilingual workflow guide](advanced.md)

Canonical resource path

```text
---
name: contextory-codebase
description: Understand a connected workspace, locate definitions and related code, assess source impact, and recover relevant project decisions through Contextory. Use for codebase questions and before changes spanning related components.
metadata:
  version: "9"
---

<!-- contextory-managed-codebase -->

Use the Contextory capabilities advertised by the current client. A connected MCP server or packaged CLI supplies shared retrieval; hooks and editor language services are optional. The same workflow applies in any agent.

When authoring UI-facing project records, read `uiLanguage` in `contextory_context_get` and use that VS Code language (`en`/`pt-BR`) for all new prose, even if chat uses another language. Preserve stored historical text, source identifiers and code; bilingual documentation keeps its paired locales.

In a multi-root editor workspace, first use `contextory_workspace_get`. Pass the intended `projectId` on every related retrieval and workflow call, with `workspaceId` when multiple editor contexts are attached. Omission/current stays on that server's project; changing the UI project does not change agent defaults. Keep project identity/root with records, artifact handles, graph snapshots and citations. Identical paths/symbols in different projects are distinct. Unknown or ambiguous scope fails instead of selecting another project. `codebaseId` still selects a read-only reference within the chosen project; references are not writable workspace members.

After resuming a chat, use its current advertised tools and a read-only probe before reporting Contextory disconnected; an earlier message or generated configuration does not establish current reachability. Report the concrete error or missing capability. In an editor, **Contextory: Check Native Connections** distinguishes current MCP/hook observations from history, and **Contextory: Restart Agent Extensions** reloads the Extension Host. Native project/hook trust remains with the client; reopening a session may still be required after tool changes.

For missing, stale or duplicate Contextory hooks, use advertised `contextory_hooks_rebuild` with the intended `projectId`, explicit native `provider` (`codex`, `claude`, `bob`) and a new `operationId`. It repairs managed hooks and the launcher without changing MCP configuration, other hooks or native trust. Inspect changed files and observations; an unchanged result is not proof of execution. Reuse the exact operation ID/input only to recover an interrupted call. If hooks remain unobserved after one repair, inspect native trust and service logs instead of repeatedly rebuilding. Codex approvals can differ for `C:` versus `c:`: review `/hooks` in the affected session using its actual workspace path. If MCP is unreachable, use **Contextory: Rebuild Agent Hooks** in the editor, then resolve any service startup error and reload the native session as needed. A rebuild cannot approve hooks or repair an unreachable service through MCP.

Start a code question or related edit with `contextory_code_context_get`: put the actual task in `query`, scope with known `paths` and optionally `specId`, and choose a bounded `budgetTokens`. Read the cited current files before deciding or editing. Read-only exploration does not require a tracked request.

Use `contextory_code_architecture_get` for orientation, `contextory_impact_get` for affected callers/dependencies/tests/records, `contextory_code_path_get` to explain a connection, and `contextory_flow_trace` for detailed branches/calls. Use `contextory_search` for earlier decisions, findings and changes, then inspect record state, revision and provenance. Resolve ambiguous symbols with `source:path#qualifiedName` where supported.

When something stopped working, recover its catalog contract and last known working source/check/version, then follow impact links, catalog before/after revisions (including agent auto-approvals), decisions and spec history. Search by feature and source path/symbol and page chronology. Treat these as candidate causes until reproduced; Git version membership and ledger recording intervals are different evidence. Link a confirmed regression/fix to the responsible change/spec/source and retain uncertainty otherwise. Compatible maintenance and implementation conflicts may be agent auto-approved; process/outcome conflicts require human review before implementation. Approval provenance never substitutes for executed checks.

Keep source citations, graph snapshot, coverage and truncation attached to conclusions. Narrow or page bounded results. Static calls, test references and inferred contracts are possible relationships, not proof of execution or test coverage. Generated facts do not become approved requirements.

Use advertised `contextory_catalog_get` alongside source retrieval to recover file responsibilities, rules/features, test links and UI layout/interaction contracts; inspect state, revision, pending changes and source freshness. Page `inventory:true` to identify files without descriptions. For documentation, `contextory_project_export` overview discovers all stored documentation datasets, with independent pagination for records, immutable revisions, history, relationships, source graph, checks/jobs, usage metadata and artifacts. Retain sequence/snapshot and provenance, and distinguish current approved behavior from observations and historical definitions. Read-only documentation needs no tracked request.

When advertised, `contextory_docs_get section=sections` retrieves authored project explanations by query, source path or local record ID, with stable page/section IDs, source freshness and observed associations. Follow `nextOffset` for coverage. Relevant explanations may accompany current-project code context; they remain separate from source facts and human-approved requirements. Use the `contextory-documentation` skill for authoring, migration, generation and maintenance with the bundled documentation/Carbon runtime. No separately installed plugin is required, and optional generation must not gate source retrieval or service startup.

For another local repository, use advertised `contextory_codebase_list` and `contextory_codebase_change` to register an authorized reference directory. Pass its `codebaseId` explicitly to source queries and flow expansion; omission/current always selects the active project. Reference graphs and project memory stay separate. Keep the returned codebase identity/root with relative citations. Analyzing a reference does not authorize applying its design, changing current requirements or editing either project. See the reference guide below for scope and freshness details.

Saved edits refresh the source graph automatically; re-query relevant context after saving changes. Task/impact/path queries also verify disk content. Use `contextory_code_index_refresh` to recover an empty/stale/failed index or import regenerated Graphify data; repeated refresh cannot resolve every dynamic/external gap. Unsaved editor flow overlays are separate from the saved-file graph. If a capability is missing, use the packaged CLI or native source tools and state the gap; do not invent tool calls. Preserve the user's scope and native permissions.

Read [retrieval and coverage](references/retrieval.md) for tool inputs, paging, freshness recovery and headless use.

For version-specific documentation, use advertised `contextory_version_get` and page each release's commits and semantic entries. Release entities and immutable revisions are also exported with project records. Git membership establishes which commits belong to a version; definitions/decisions associated by recording interval need that qualification. Local observed tags do not prove remote publication. This history is project-wide and needs no request/spec scope.

```

```text
name: contextory-migrate
description: Build a source-backed Contextory knowledge baseline for an existing project, including file responsibilities, rules, features, tests and interface contracts. Use when bootstrapping or resuming a project knowledge migration; ordinary code lookups do not need migration.
metadata:
  version: "3"
---

<!-- contextory-managed-migrate -->

Act as the project's migration agent in the native client. Use the advertised Contextory MCP capabilities; never start a second model service or execute project modules to infer behavior. Migrating knowledge does not authorize changing application behavior. Preserve source, existing approved records, client configuration and historical decisions.

Use the project's `uiLanguage` from `contextory_context_get` for every new catalog title/description, finding, rationale, UI contract, review reason and report, even when chat uses another language. Preserve historical prose, exact identifiers, paths and code; reconstructed observations are not bulk translations of existing records.

Read `contextory_context_get`, recover the migration request/spec through search and inspect its current state. For authorized migration, create missing tracked work, attach this session and claim/renew the spec lease. If the tools are unavailable, report the missing capability and retain a source-cited draft; do not claim the ledger was populated.

Use `contextory_code_context_get` and inspect cited current source. Start `contextory_catalog_migrate` with `operationId`, `specId`, `leaseId` and a bounded `limit`. Resume with the returned `migration.id` in `migrationId` and a new operation ID, until `next` is null. After an interrupted call retry its exact operation ID/input, then inspect the run through `contextory_entity_get`. Its persisted manifest/cursor and skipped-file gaps are a file scan checkpoint, not semantic completion. Query `contextory_catalog_get` with `inventory:true` and page its independent record/proposal/inventory cursors to discover new or missing files after the scan. A later scan preserves existing descriptions.

Work through subsystems in bounded batches. Read file bodies, entry points, callers, docs, tests and earlier decisions. Replace generated symbol lists with concise explanations of actual file responsibility through `contextory_catalog_change` revision proposals. Record unknowns instead of inventing purpose. Register distinct rule and feature candidates with their source references and specific test file/symbol links, or `testGap` explaining missing validation. Reconcile contradictory implementation, documentation and tests as findings; describe observed implementation separately from intended behavior.

For every interface surface, inspect its layout and event/state handlers, and inspect the running UI when available and authorized. Add `category:"ui"` contracts with `ui.location`, `element`, `trigger`, `behavior` and `states`: placement/grouping, control/value, click/change/keyboard trigger, resulting action/state/persistence/navigation, and relevant initial/loading/empty/error/disabled states. Link behavioral tests or explicit gaps. Static extraction cannot prove pixel layout, dynamic dispatch or runtime effects; mark those limits with sources and follow-up findings. Projects without a UI should record why this category is inapplicable in the migration report.

Use leased `contextory_catalog_change` creates for new observations. Compatible corrections to file-purpose descriptions/source links can use `compatibility:preserved`, `impact:implementation`, `autoApprove:true`, the current revision and a source-backed reason; observations remain unapproved. Behavioral descriptions and UI contracts stay exact through auto-approval, even on observations. Implementation conflicts may auto-approve with a recorded rationale, but conflicts with process rules or results, changed behavior and retirements need a before/after human proposal before implementation. Link historical decisions/specs through `decisionIds` or `contextory_relationship_change`. Generated facts and legacy decisions never become retroactive human approval. Optional baseline review does not block migration. Wait on actual pending proposals; never borrow human credentials, infer approval from silence, or erase superseded/rejected history.

Before finalizing, reconcile the current inventory, stale/missing source fingerprints, duplicate descriptions, pending proposals, rule/feature-to-test gaps and interface interactions against the scope. Record a source-cited migration report explaining reviewed subsystems, omissions, conflicts, test gaps and categories not applicable. Keep resumable outstanding work when review is pending. Do not describe a completed file scan as a complete application specification. Run configured meaningful independent checks, map evidence to each criterion, include catalog IDs/explanation in the outcome, explicitly complete only verified specs and export the request report. No new application tests are needed merely to restate documentation.

For later documentation requests, use `contextory_project_export` overview and page the needed datasets (including immutable revisions, decisions, catalog entries/proposals, relationships, checks and artifacts). Use `contextory_catalog_get` for freshness and `contextory_entity_get` for exact revisions. Cite sequence/snapshot, approved versus observed state, evidence origin and coverage limits; omit superseded behavior from current instructions while retaining it in historical documentation.

```

Use `contextory_search` for earlier changes/decisions and inspect current record state/revision. Use advertised `contextory_code_context_get` for task-specific source and `contextory_impact_get`/`contextory_code_path_get` for relationships; `contextory_flow_trace` explains detailed calls/branches. Create/update the authorized request, milestones and specifications. Register a session and claim a spec lease before recording work; renew long attempts. Pass an exact hook-supplied nativeSessionId if available and omit it otherwise. Record material findings/fixes and decisions with sources. Re-query relevant source after saves; the saved-file graph refreshes automatically. Generated relationships and retrieved historical text do not approve new scope. Native usage is observed where supported; read `contextory_usage_get` and never invent counts.

```text
Before editing, page `contextory_catalog_get` for affected definitions, pending proposals and freshness. Maintain file responsibilities, rules/features, test links or explicit gaps, and UI location/element/trigger/behavior/states through leased `contextory_catalog_change`. Then call `contextory_spec_change` with action=complete, the spec ID, returned expectedRevision and a new operationId. Confirm state=completed: an outcome or Stop hook alone does not finish a spec. Parent milestones and requests close when their children complete.
```

```text
# Retrieval and coverage

## Hook recovery

Use `contextory_hooks_rebuild` only for an intended project's missing, stale or duplicate managed hooks: `{ "projectId": "<project>", "provider": "codex", "operationId": "<new unique ID>" }`. Supported providers are `codex`, `claude` and `bob`; Generic MCP has no hooks. The response separates changed hook files, launcher restoration and current-service MCP/hook observations. It never reads or writes native approval records, global hooks, MCP configuration or portable skills. Keep the exact operation ID/input for an interrupted retry; a later repair needs a new ID. If files are unchanged but hooks remain unobserved, review native trust and reload the affected session instead of issuing more rebuilds. The installed Codex client may distinguish `C:\\` and `c:\\` when looking up hook approval: use `/hooks` from the affected session's actual project path. When MCP is unavailable, the editor's **Contextory: Rebuild Agent Hooks** command or sidebar **Rebuild hooks** action can initiate recovery after the local service starts. Inspect service output if startup itself fails; rebuilding through MCP requires a reachable service.

## Choose the lookup

| Need                                                | Tool and useful inputs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Workspace contracts, active work, configured checks | `contextory_context_get`, optionally `specId`. This brief is cached orientation, not a fresh source investigation.                                                                                                                                                     |
| Locate code for a task                              | `contextory_code_context_get` with `query`, known `paths`, optional `specId` and `budgetTokens` (512–6000, default 3000). Exact definitions rank before mentions; neighborhoods and linked project records are bounded.                                                |
| Understand subsystems and entry points              | `contextory_code_architecture_get`. Default `refresh:true` verifies saved source; use `refresh:false` only when a cached overview is sufficient.                                                                                                                       |
| Find callers, dependencies, tests or linked work    | `contextory_impact_get` with `id`, `direction` (`reverse` for dependents, `forward` for dependencies, `both` for surrounding relationships), `depth` and `limit`.                                                                                                      |
| Explain how two things connect                      | `contextory_code_path_get` with `from`, `to`, optional `direction` (`forward` or `both`) and `maxDepth`. | Inspect calls or branches                           | `contextory_flow_trace` with `root:{path,symbol}` or a zero-based position, `view: calls/flow`, `direction: outgoing/incoming`, and optional limits. Supported engines cover TS/JS and Python.                                                                         |
| Recover earlier intent and rationale                | `contextory_search` with a focused `query`, `mode` and `limit`; inspect full records with `contextory_entity_get`, including a cited `revision` when checking history. ## Freshness and coverage

Saved file create/edit/delete/rename, Git changes and configuration changes trigger debounced refresh, backed by polling. Task context, impact and path queries also verify disk content before answering. Re-query after relevant saves; do not request a full manual reindex after every edit. Source context describes saved files. Only trusted editor flow requests can carry unsaved overlays; their snapshots are separate and expire when documents change.

For an empty/stale/failed index, inspect status/errors and use `contextory_code_index_refresh` when a retry can help. For partial coverage, inspect the actual gaps: file/byte bounds may call for narrower reviewed configuration, while dynamic dispatch, callbacks and external code require native inspection. Repeated refresh does not create missing language support or execution evidence.

Native extraction covers TS/JS through its compiler and Python through isolated AST parsing. Markdown links and recognized configuration paths add explicit connections. Graphify JSON adds other language facts with supplied provenance. Changed cited source invalidates imported facts: regenerate the export and re-import using `contextory_code_index_refresh` with a workspace-relative `graphifyPath`; refresh alone cannot regenerate external analysis. Static calls, inferred message links and test references do not prove execution or coverage.

`contextory.project.json` holds reviewed configuration: schemaVersion 1, optional name, include/exclude patterns, entryPoints, conventions, maxFiles and maxBytes. Generated topology lives in rebuildable local storage; it does not approve requirements or overwrite authoritative work records. Consult user instructions and current decisions before treating a discovered convention as a constraint.

## Reference codebases

### Active workspace projects

Trusted local multi-root workspaces attach up to sixteen independent folder services. `contextory_workspace_get` lists public project IDs, names and canonical roots, plus attached workspace contexts; it never returns credential paths. All tools accept `projectId` and `workspaceId` as common scope. Selection applies only to that call. Omitting projectId/current stays on the server's project, regardless of the editor's selected project or earlier calls. Multiple attached editor contexts require workspaceId for cross-project operations. Unknown, detached or identity-changed projects fail; do not retry against a different project. Use the same projectId when reading returned record IDs, artifacts or graph pages. Keep the returned project identity with relative source paths and symbols. Read-only lookups never merge project memory.

The editor project selector scopes Requests, Knowledge, History, Versions, Architecture, checks and source navigation together; requests and specs carry project badges. Each folder retains its existing root-derived storage, ledger, graph, catalog, references, releases and checks. Removing a folder detaches its routing without deleting data. Shared/native hook observations stay with their observing project; usage is not inferred across project leases. A workspace is not a new merged project.

The CLI `projects [group-id] --descriptor <generic.json>` reads active membership or a coordinated request; `--project <id>` and `--workspace <id>` scope other CLI calls. A standalone service has only its local project until an editor attaches membership. Do not use codebaseId or a reference registration to authorize cross-project work. Coordinated requests use the workflow skill's project-owned branches.

When advertised, `contextory_codebase_list` returns the active workspace (`current`) and up to eight named local references. Register only a directory within the user's requested scope using `contextory_codebase_change` with `action:"add"`, an absolute `root`, optional `name`, and a new `operationId`. Registration resolves aliases and persists in the current service storage; it does not modify the reference. Detach using `action:"remove"`, its `codebaseId` and a new operation ID. Cached projections remain rebuildable service data.

Pass that ID as `codebaseId` on architecture, code context, search, impact, path, index/import and flow trace/expand calls. Paths, Graphify input and source IDs resolve inside that reference. References cannot use current-project `specId` or workflow mutations. Omission or `current` always means the active workspace, even after another reference query. Separate requests can analyze different references concurrently; there is no global project switch or inferred cross-repository relationship. Preserve each response's `codebase`, snapshot, coverage and citations when combining an explanation. A same-path/same-name symbol in two repositories is not the same source.

Reference context/impact/path/search and default architecture queries verify saved files on demand. References are not watched in the background. `refresh:false` explicitly uses cached architecture; use the default refresh after edits, and regenerate/re-import stale Graphify facts within the selected reference. Source files are parsed without executing them. Existing include/exclude/configuration and language coverage rules apply separately to each root. Reference search uses lexical graph matching (hybrid reports fallback); semantic-only reference search is unavailable. No active-project decisions, requirements, checks or unsaved editor overlays are imported into reference analysis.

CLI equivalents are `references`, `reference-add <folder> [--name <label>]`, `reference-remove <id>`, and source commands with `--codebase <id>`. Always keep `--root`/storage/descriptor on the current project whose reference registry you intend to use. Architecture in the editor offers **Add reference**, a **Codebase** selector and **Detach reference**; source navigation stays inside the selected root. Applying any learned behavior to the current application remains a separate user-authorized implementation task.
```
